newsitem.title: USA: Factory Card Outlet June sales recover.
newsitem.headline: Factory Card Outlet June sales recover.

text.p: Factory Card Outlet Corp, which had warned that lower April and May sales would cause its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter results to fall short of expectations, said it has addressed the issues and June same store sales are running ahead of last year.

"In the month of June so far, we have taken the card business from a negative comp (comparable store sales) in April and May to a slightly positive comp," President Charles Cumello told a Piper Jaffray investment conference here. He added that June same store sales so far are up about five percent from a year ago.

Cumello said the company has made changes in its direct mail program and has its store openings back on track. And a newly installed point-of-sale system will allow the company to track merchandise more effectively, he added.

Earlier this month, the company estimated sales for its fiscal fourth quarter to end June 28, 1997 in a range of $39 million to $40 million, up from $31 million generated a year ago, but below the company's previous estimate of $43 million.

Fiscal fourth quarter earnings were estimated at $0.22 to $0.25 a share, down from a consensus analyst estimate of $0.34. At that time, the company said actual earnings will depend on sales during the rest of June and the level of inventory shrinkage.
For its fiscal year, Factory Card Outlet had estimated earnings at $0.18 to $0.22, compared with a consensus analyst estimate of $0.33. The company earned $0.01 in fiscal 1996.
At that time, the company attributed the sales shortfall to timing of some direct mail advertising, opening of some stores later than planned, and some merchandise issues.
The company also said that these were correctable issues and that its business remained fundamentally strong.
Factory Card Outlet expects to open about 50 stores next year and sees the chain growing to 1,000 stores over time. The Bensenville, Ill.-based firm now has 140 stores in 18 states.

"We are looking to open 50 or so superstores a year," Cumello said in an interview after the presentation. He said the company could accelerate that growth rate or acquire another company in the fragmented and consolidating industry.
"This is a young industry. There are a five or six chains out there, and a couple of smaller regional chains. I think there will be consolidation," he said.
Longer term, Cumello said, "We think we have the opportunity of a 1,000 store chain over time."

The company owns all of its stores and has no plans to franchise units as competitor Party City does. "I don't think we ever would (offer franchises). There is much better control. The company typically is much more profitable if you do it right and you don't have to deal with those other issues," he said.

Factory Card Outlet, which went public in December 1996, sells party supplies, greeting cards, gift wrap and special occasion merchandise usually at 20 to 60 percent off regular prices. It offers a choice of 4,000 greeting cards at 39 cents each.
Factory Card Outlet shares were up 1/16 at 5-7/8 Thursday.
